([[New York City, New York]]) | college = * [[Monroe Community College|Monroe CC]] (2019–2020) * [[Chipola College]] (2020–2022) * [[Kansas State Wildcats men's basketball|Kansas State]] (2022–2023) * [[Memphis Tigers men's basketball|Memphis]] (2023–2024) | draft_year = 2024 | career_start = 2024 | career_end = | years1 = [[2024–25 NBA G League season|2024–2025]] | team1 = [[Cleveland Charge]] | years2 = {{nbay|2024|end}}–present | team2 = [[Cleveland Cavaliers]] | years3 = [[2024–25 NBA G League season|2025]]–[[2025–26 NBA G League season|2026]] | team3 = →Cleveland Charge | highlights = }} '''Nae'Qwan Tomlin''' (born December 19, 2000) is an American professional [[basketball]] player for the [[Cleveland Cavaliers]] of the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA). He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Monroe Community College|Monroe CC Tribunes]], [[Chipola College|Chipola Indians]], [[Kansas State Wildcats men's basketball|Kansas State Wildcats]] and the [[Memphis Tigers men's basketball|Memphis Tigers]]. ==Early life== Tomlin was born in [[Brooklyn]], New York.{{cite web |last=Spears |first=Marc J. |title=Inside Nae’Qwan Tomlin’s unique path to the Cleveland Cavaliers |url=https://andscape.com/features/inside-naeqwan-tomlins-unique-path-to-the-cleveland-cavaliers/ |website=Andscape |access-date=January 28, 2026 |date=January 28, 2026}} He moved to [[Harlem]] with his mother, Aisha Ismael, when he was aged 10. Tomlin became a fan of basketball through his mother who watched games on television. Tomlin attended Urban Assembly High School in [[New York City]]. He did not take his academics seriously and poor grades prevented him from making the basketball team during his only attempt as a senior. Tomlin played at [[Rucker Park]] where he played in a prep league and was noticed by Torrell Harris, the father of basketball player [[Tobias Harris]]. Harris sent Tomlin to [[San Antonio]] so he could attend Strength N Motion International, a prep school led by [[George Gervin]]. Tomlin learned fundamental basketball skills and guidance from Gervin. Harris then helped Tomlin to enroll at [[Monroe Community College]] in New York. ==College career== [[File:Nae'Quan Tomlin Dec 2022.png|thumb|Tomlin with the [[Kansas State Wildcats men's basketball|Kansas State Wildcats]] in 2022]] Tomlin played for the [[Monroe Community College|Monroe CC Tribunes]] during the 2019–20 season for what was his first stint of organized basketball. He averaged 13.3 points, 8.8 rebounds and 3.3 blocks per game. Tomlin then played for the [[Chipola College|Chipola Indians]] from 2020 to 2022 and led the team to a combined 53–11 record. Afterwards, Tomlin transferred to the [[Kansas State Wildcats men's basketball|Kansas State Wildcats]], helping the team advance to the Elite Eight in [[2023 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|2023]]. On December 6, 2023, Tomlin was dismissed from Kansas State after being suspended indefinitely following an arrest for disorderly conduct.{{cite web | last=Green | first=PJ | title=Nae'Qwan Tomlin dismissed from K-State basketball | website=Yahoo! Sports | date=2023-12-07 | url=https://sports.yahoo.com/nae-qwan-tomlin-dismissed-k-011608630.html | access-date=2025-12-05}} In his final season, he transferred mid-season to the [[Memphis Tigers men's basketball|Memphis Tigers]], playing 21 games and averaging 14 points and 6 rebounds, the latter the second most on the team.{{cite web |last=Hilliard |first=Caleb |date=June 29, 2024 |title=Nae'Qwan Tomlin Inks Contract with the Cleveland Cavaliers
